guidelineReference: SJA First Aid / burn care and shock
title: Severe cooking oil scalds in a food van
setting: Christmas light switch-on. A 28M food van worker was splashed with boiling cooking oil. Severe partial thickness burns over both hands, arms, and neck.
verdictExplanation: Boiling oil burns covering a large surface area (hands, arms, neck) with severe pain, borderline low BP (85/58), and high risk of shock/airway swelling. Sick: 999.

shared.response: Alert and responsive, in extreme distress
shared.circulation: Red, blistered skin over hands, arms, and neck; elevated pulse

history.history: Splashed with boiling oil from a deep fryer 5 minutes ago inside a fish and chip van
history.injuries: Partial thickness blistered burns over hands, bilateral forearms, and lower neck
history.additional: Van is hot and humid, nearest tap is 100m away

followUp.question: What is your immediate management for these severe scalds?

options.text: Call 999, cool the affected areas with cool running water for 20 minutes, remove jewelry, and cover loosely
Apply ice packs directly to the burns to cool them as fast as possible
Apply a thick layer of antiseptic cream and wrap tightly in a heavy elastic bandage
Do nothing; oil burns do not need water as oil and water do not mix

followUp.explanation: Severe large-area burns require an immediate 999 call. Cool with clean, cool running water for 20 minutes. Remove rings/watches before swelling begins. Cover burns loosely with cling film or sterile dressings. Never use ice (causes tissue frostbite) or greasy creams.

evolvingStage.narrative: While waiting for the ambulance and continuing to cool the burns, the patient's voice becomes hoarse and he develops stridor (a harsh vibrating noise when breathing). He complains of tightness in his throat and is struggling to breathe.

followUp.question: What is the most likely cause of this deterioration and what is your priority?

options.text: Airway swelling and impending obstruction secondary to burns around the neck and face; sit the patient upright, give high-flow oxygen, and immediately update EMS
Hypovolaemic shock due to severe fluid loss; lay the patient flat, raise legs if possible, keep warm, and update EMS
Anaphylaxis to the cooking oil; administer an auto-injector if available
A panic attack due to the pain; offer reassurance and a paper bag to breathe into

followUp.explanation: Burns to the neck/face and inhalation of steam/hot oil can cause rapid and fatal airway swelling. The patient must be kept upright to optimize breathing, administered high-flow oxygen, and EMS immediately updated regarding this critical deterioration.

levelFlags.cfaNotes: Call 999 immediately. Cool under running water. Remove jewelry. Reassure the patient.
levelFlags.erNotes: Large partial thickness scalds (>10% TBSA risk). Cool for 20 minutes, remove jewelry, administer high-flow oxygen, check BGL, assess airway for inhalation/neck swelling, keep patient warm during cooling (risk of hypothermia), and expedite priority transfer.
